sources.note: GFPO samples a larger group of rollouts per problem during RL training and updates only on the top-k by length or by reward-per-token, converting extra training-time compute into shorter responses at inference.
sources.title: Sample More to Think Less: Group Filtered Policy Optimization for Concise Reasoning

sources.note: FROST uses attention weights to identify and prune sentence-level 'reasoning outliers' from a reasoning model's chain of thought, reporting an average 69.68% token reduction and 26.70% accuracy gain over the base model on four maths benchmarks.
sources.title: FROST: Filtering Reasoning Outliers with Attention for Efficient Reasoning

result.definition: Phi-4-reasoning is a reasoning language model that archived papers evaluate on, not a concept, method or dataset; the wiki has no kind for a model, so it is filed under the least wrong of the three available. GFPO uses it as its sole base model and measures reduction in GRPO's excess length rather than raw length: Shortest-8/16 cuts 23.7%-36.5% across AIME 24/25, GPQA, Omni-MATH and LiveCodeBench, Token Efficiency GFPO cuts 70.9%-84.6%, and Adaptive Difficulty GFPO cuts 35.1%-52.9%, with no statistically significant accuracy difference from GRPO. FROST prunes attention-identified 'reasoning outliers' from its chain of thought and reports GSM8K 93.11% at 154.33 tokens, MATH500 59.80% at 344.37, AIME24 26.67% at 899.80 and Minerva 27.16% at 401.19, alongside a 15.97% drop in maximum attention infinity norm and 91.09% in average kurtosis. Both papers treat it as a reasoning model whose chains are long enough to be worth shortening; neither describes how it was trained.
